# Third-Party Integrations — Glow Menu Component

Every external service, platform, and library this project is wired into — what is configured, what is merely installed, and how to extend it.

---

## 1. v0.app — AI Generation + Git Sync (CONFIGURED)

**Status: active and configured.** This repository was generated by [v0.app](https://v0.app) and stays in sync with its v0 project.

### How it works

1. The app is designed and modified in the v0 chat interface: **[v0.app/chat/projects/m4E6cfee2qC](https://v0.app/chat/projects/m4E6cfee2qC)**
2. Deploying from the v0 interface automatically pushes changes to this GitHub repository.
3. Vercel deploys the latest commit from this repository.

### Evidence in the codebase

- `README.md` — v0 boilerplate with sync badges.
- `app/layout.tsx` — `export const metadata = { generator: 'v0.app' };` stamps every page's metadata with the generator.
- `components.json` — shadcn configuration as generated by the v0 scaffold.
- `next.config.mjs` — `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds` + `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors` are v0 defaults chosen so AI-generated code always builds.

### Caveats for developers

- **v0 can overwrite your local edits.** If you edit files locally and someone (or a scheduled sync) redeploys from the v0 chat, the v0 version wins. For a fork you own, either stop editing in v0 or treat v0 as the source of truth and pull after each v0 change.
- The v0 project link in the old README points at a specific user's project; if you forked this repo, create your own v0 project or delete the v0 references.

---

## 2. Vercel — Hosting + Deployment (CONFIGURED)

**Status: configured as the deployment target.** The live site for the original v0 project is on Vercel.

### What Vercel provides here

- **Git-triggered deploys:** every push to the connected branch produces a preview/production deployment.
- **Edge network + TLS:** HTTPS and global CDN with zero configuration.
- **Build settings:** framework preset "Next.js", build command `pnpm build` (or `next build`), install command `pnpm install`. Defaults work — nothing custom is needed.

### What is NOT configured on Vercel for this project

- **No environment variables** (the app needs none — see `docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md`). If you add any later, set them in **Project Settings → Environment Variables**, not in the repo.
- **No custom domain** in the repo config (domains are attached in the Vercel dashboard).
- **No Vercel Analytics dashboard wiring in code.**

### Deploying this repo yourself

1. Push the repo to GitHub.
2. In Vercel: **Add New → Project → Import** the repo.
3. Accept the detected Next.js preset. No env vars are required.
4. Deploy. Every future push redeploys automatically.

> **Static-export alternative:** with `images.unoptimized: true` already set, adding `output: "export"` to `next.config.mjs` would let this deploy as pure static files on any host (Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Netlify). See `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.

## 3. Vercel Analytics — INSTALLED, NOT WIRED (action required if wanted)

**Status: the `@vercel/analytics@1.3.1` package is installed but never imported.** A `grep` across all source files finds zero references to `Analytics` or `@vercel/analytics`.

### What this means

- The dependency downloads and bundles nothing today — it's dead weight in `package.json`.
- No page-view or Web-Vitals data is being collected, even on the Vercel deployment.

### To actually enable it

In `app/layout.tsx`, add:

```tsx
import { Analytics } from "@vercel/analytics/react";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body className={inter.className}>
        <ThemeProvider attribute="class" defaultTheme="light" disableSystemTheme>
          {children}
        </ThemeProvider>
        <Analytics />
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

No API key or env var is needed — `@vercel/analytics` auto-configures from the Vercel project. If you don't want analytics, remove the package (`pnpm remove @vercel/analytics`) instead of leaving it installed-but-dead.

## 4. Library Integrations (npm packages, configured in code)

These are third-party libraries actively used by the source code:

| Library | Version | Used in | Purpose |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| `framer-motion` | `latest` | `components/menu-bar.tsx` | All animation: 3D flip variants (`rotateX`), glow scale/spring, nav-bar radial glow. The entire menu interaction is Framer Motion variants + `whileHover`. |
| `next-themes` | `latest` | `components/theme-provider.tsx`, `components/theme-toggle.tsx`, `components/menu-bar.tsx` | Theme state (`useTheme`), `.dark` class management on `<html>`. `disableSystemTheme` is set, so the toggle is purely manual with `defaultTheme="light"`. |
| `lucide-react` | `^0.454.0` | `menu-bar.tsx` (Home, Bell, Settings, User), `theme-toggle.tsx` (Sun, Moon) | Icon set. Tree-shaken per-icon imports. |
| `@radix-ui/react-switch` (via shadcn) | `1.1.2` | `components/ui/switch.tsx` → `theme-toggle.tsx` | Accessible switch primitive behind the theme toggle. The other 23 `@radix-ui/*` packages are installed but unused by the current pages. |
| `next/font/google` | (built into Next) | `app/layout.tsx` | Loads the **Inter** font (`subsets: ["latin"]`), applied to `<body>`. Self-hosted by Next at build time — no runtime request to Google Fonts. |
| `geist` | `^1.3.1` | `styles/globals.css` (`--font-sans`/`--font-mono` vars) | Geist font CSS variables. Declared in CSS but the layout actually applies Inter; Geist vars are available for use. |
| `tailwindcss` + `tailwindcss-animate` | `^3.4.17` / `^1.0.7` | everywhere | Utility styling + accordion keyframes. |
| `clsx` / `tailwind-merge` / `class-variance-authority` | — | `lib/utils.ts`, `ui/switch.tsx` | The standard shadcn `cn()` helper for merging class names. |

### Installed but unused

Beyond `@vercel/analytics`, these packages are in `package.json` but have no imports in the current source: all `@radix-ui/*` packages except `react-switch`, `@hookform/resolvers`, `cmdk`, `date-fns`, `embla-carousel-react`, `input-otp`, `react-day-picker`, `react-hook-form`, `react-resizable-panels`, `recharts`, `sonner`, `vaul`, `zod`, `@emotion/is-prop-valid`. They are v0-scaffold leftovers so any component you add from the shadcn set works without installing anything. Safe to prune with `pnpm remove` if you want a lean install.

---

## 5. Adding a New Third-Party Integration — Playbook

1. **Install:** `pnpm add <package>` (never `npm install` — keep the single pnpm lockfile).
2. **Secrets:** if it needs a key, follow `docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md` — `.env.local` locally, Vercel dashboard in production, `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix only if client code reads it.
3. **Client vs. server:** anything using browser APIs, `useState`, or event handlers needs `"use client"` at the top of the file (see `menu-bar.tsx`).
4. **Analytics-style snippets:** prefer the official React package over pasting `<script>` tags; if a script tag is unavoidable, use `next/script` with an explicit `strategy`.
5. **Document it here:** add a section above with status, where it's configured, and what would break if removed.
